info.title: Swarmail
info.description: The fastest AI-native SMTP mail mock. Accepts any SMTP traffic on :1025, answers POP3 (RFC 1939 core + TOP/CAPA) on :1110 with the inbox as the maildrop, and exposes captured email through this API on :8025 — including MailHog/Mailpit-compatible read endpoints. Every accepted message is queryable immediately — there is no async gap where mail can be lost.

Prometheus metrics

LLM-oriented quick reference

post.description: initialize, tools/list, tools/call. The stdio transport is available via `swarmail mcp`. Every error is a JSON-RPC error object (decision 0044 §1): malformed JSON or invalid UTF-8 is HTTP 400 -32700; a body over 2097152 bytes is HTTP 413 -32600 naming the limit; a value that is not an object is -32600 with a null id, once per such batch member; an object without an id is a notification that runs and gets no reply only when its method is a string — any other id-less object is -32600 with a null id (proposed 0047 §3). A batch holds 1 to 16 members, polled concurrently: replies keep member order, member effects have no order. Every tool refuses an argument key its inputSchema does not publish (-32602, additionalProperties: false).

413.description: -32600 body over the 2097152-byte limit, null id

get.summary: Long-poll until `count` messages match the filter (push-based wait, no sleep-polling)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Any recipient, envelope included (see the list's `to`)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size for the returned matches — the same shape list takes (decision 0029 §1)

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Minimum one — a count of 0 still waits for at least one matching message (decision 0010)

parameters.name: timeout_ms
parameters.description: Above 60000 the request is refused with 400, never clamped (decision 0018)

200.description: Matched — `total` is counted after the wait, describing the response's observed state (decision 0018)

400.description: `timeout_ms` above 60000 — refused, never clamped (decision 0018); a blank inbox, or an unknown query key such as `offset`, named — no waiter is registered (decision 0044 §3)

503.description: The server is stopping — the wait answers `{"error":"shutting down"}` instead of parking (decision 0018)

get.summary: Assert an exact match count (200 when equal, 409 with expected/matched otherwise)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Any recipient, envelope included: `to=bcc@x&count=0` fails when the address was a Bcc envelope recipient — this is not a header-presence assertion

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Parsed for parity with list (decision 0029 §1) but inert: the assert answer is a count, not a page

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Exact match count — 0 asserts the filtered inbox is empty; the count is never clamped to one

400.description: A blank inbox, a malformed value or an unknown query key — a misspelled filter refuses by name instead of vanishing (decision 0044 §3)

get.summary: Thread view of an inbox (newest thread first)
get.description: Mails are grouped into conversations by their References/In-Reply-To/Message-ID chains, falling back, for mail with no chain at all, to the normalized subject (leading Re/Fw/Fwd/Aw/SV/VS/Antw/WG/TR/RV/Odp/R/I/ENC/RES/Ответ/回复 markers stripped with an ASCII or full-width colon, whitespace runs collapsed, case-folded; a numbered Re[2]: stays literal). Each thread lists its mails oldest first. Capped at 200 mails.

get.summary: One thread by its key (the conversation, oldest first)

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The thread's stable key, as returned by the threads list

get.summary: Live inbox feed (server-sent events)
get.description: One `threads` event per change, carrying the full thread view (the GET /threads shape) as JSON. The first event is the snapshot; a watcher that falls behind is repaired with a recomputed view, never an error. Subscribes before the first scan, so mail landing while the client connects is pushed, not missed.

post.summary: Inject a synthetic email (full parse/extract pipeline runs)
post.description: Builds the fixture through the same seed constructor the MCP `swarmail_seed_email` tool uses (decision 0010). When `html` is given it is preserved verbatim under `Content-Type: text/html` and supersedes `text`; extraction (links, codes) runs at ingest. Envelope fields containing CR, LF or NUL are refused before anything is stored.

400.description: Refused fixture — an envelope field (to, from or subject) contains CR, LF or NUL; nothing was stored

503.description: `storage commit failed` — the commit refused, nothing was stored (decision 0012); during shutdown the boundary refuses before any commit with the same text (decision 0024)

get.summary: MailHog/Mailpit list shape over the whole store (Mailpit's summary envelope, newest first)
get.description: The Mailpit `/api/v1/messages` shape: {total, unread, count, messages_count, messages_unread, start, tags, messages}. No query names a mailbox: the whole store is one global mailbox, as both tools expose it. `?inbox=` scopes to a single swarmail inbox (a blank one is a 400); `?limit=`/`?start=` page. Each Snippet is built from at most the first 8192 bytes of its body; the page is built off the async workers.

delete.description: Body `{"ids":[...]}` — a non-empty array of message ids — deletes exactly those messages and replies `{"removed": n}`. Every other body (absent, empty, unparseable, wrong-typed, or an empty `ids` array) is answered `400` and deletes nothing; the cross-inbox wipe is `DELETE /api/v1/delete-all`.

400.description: No usable selector — nothing was deleted

503.description: `storage commit failed` — the first refused commit ends the batch; ids already committed in this request stay deleted and a retry is idempotent (decision 0014's per-mutation refusal, not batch atomicity); during shutdown the boundary refuses before any commit with the same text (decision 0024)

get.summary: Mailpit's full message shape
Mailpit's full message shape for the newest mail in scope (issues #55, #95)
get.description: The same shape as `GET /api/v1/message/{id}`, over the newest mail by receive time then id — not commit sequence; concurrent parses can insert out of arrival order (decision 0044 §4). `?inbox=` scopes to one inbox; no inbox is the whole store. A nonblank `?query=` is refused with 400: search, then fetch the id. Two calls are two snapshots.

200.description: Mailpit MessageSummary envelope; kind=from matches the SMTP envelope sender

400.description: Missing query, unknown kind, a blank inbox, or field syntax in a containing query: every whitespace-separated word opening with an identifier and a colon (`to:x`, `foo:x`) is refused by name, a URL's `://` excepted (decision 0044 §7)

get.summary: MailHog v2 list shape over the whole store
get.description: {total, count, start, items} where items are MailHog data.Message objects (Content.{Headers,Body,Size,MIME}, Raw.{From,To,Data,Helo}); From and Raw.From are the SMTP envelope sender. `?inbox=` scopes; `?limit=`/`?start=` page. The page is serialized off the async workers into one buffer capped at 67108864 bytes of actual JSON (decision 0044 §6).

400.description: An over-cap limit, a blank inbox, or `compat page exceeds byte budget 67108864; reduce limit or fetch raw by id` — the whole page refused, nothing partial sent; one large mail can exceed it even at limit=1

get.summary: MailHog v2 search

400.description: Bare 400 (no body) for an unknown kind, an absent kind, or an empty query, as upstream answers; a JSON error naming an over-cap limit, a blank inbox, field syntax in a containing query, or the 67108864-byte page budget

delete.summary: swarmail's own explicit wipe of every inbox — not an upstream route; MailHog's bodyless DELETE /api/v1/messages is refused (decision 0011)

Raw RFC 5322 source
Current chaos rules

put.summary: Replace chaos rules (event: connect|mail_from|rcpt|data; probability 0-100; optional error line and delay_ms)

400.description: A rule outside its domain refused, never stored; the active rules are unchanged (issues #32/#41, decisions 0025/0029). Sentences: "probability must be an integer between 0 and 100", "error must be a single-line 4xx/5xx SMTP reply of at most 510 octets" (a 2xx error is refused), "delay_ms must be an integer between 0 and 300000". A body with an unknown event or rule key is 422.

get.summary: Current webhook targets (the secret is redacted: null)
get.description: The targets redacted (decision 0029 §5, amended by 0041 §3): every secret is null and every URL loses its userinfo (http://user:pw@host/x is shown as http://host/x; delivery still sends the credentials). Query, fragment, inbox and ca_pem are shown as stored. PUT is the only writer and an operator retains their own payload.

put.summary: Replace webhook targets. Each delivery POSTs {event:"received", email:{...}} with X-Swarmail-Secret; retried 4x (100ms..1.6s). http:// and https:// targets (https over TLS via reqwest + rustls, verification on; optional per-target ca_pem), dialed directly: environment proxies are ignored and redirects are not followed. The 200 echo is redacted like GET.

400.description: A target that cannot be delivered is refused before any effect (issue #47, decision 0029 §5): the body names the defect, e.g. "webhook target 0: webhook URL must name a host" (a scheme-forgotten localhost:9000), an unsupported scheme, an unparsable URL, a ca_pem that does not load, or a secret that is not an HTTP header value of at most 4096 octets without leading or trailing space or tab (decision 0041 §1). No refusal echoes the secret or the URL. Nothing is applied: the previous target list stays in place.

envelope_from.description: The SMTP MAIL FROM reverse path, captured at ingest: "" for a bounce's null sender <>, null only for mail stored before it was kept — never backfilled from the header From (decision 0044 §8)

recipients.description: The envelope recipients (RCPT TO), Bcc included; the `to` filter matches these as well as the To/Cc headers

message_id.description: The Message-ID header value, angle brackets stripped; absent when the mail has none

in_reply_to.description: The first In-Reply-To id; absent when the mail has none

references.description: The References ids in header order; absent when the mail has none

key.description: Stable short key (16 hex chars) usable in URLs and the thread endpoint

subject.description: The newest mail's display subject; absent when no mail in the thread has one

SeedRequest.description: Fixture body. `html` is preserved verbatim and supersedes `text` when both are given. `to`, `from` and `subject` refuse CR, LF and NUL. An omitted optional field takes its default; a present null or non-string is refused with 422 naming the field (decision 0044 §3). The stored mail's envelope_from is the seed's from.

from.description: Defaults to fixture@swarmail.dev; refuses CR, LF and NUL

to.description: The recipient envelope address; refuses CR, LF and NUL

subject.description: Defaults to (no subject); refuses CR, LF and NUL

text.description: Plain-text body; ignored when html is given

html.description: HTML body, preserved verbatim under Content-Type: text/html; supersedes text

probability.description: Percentage chance the event fires. Outside 0-100 the PUT is refused with 400 — probability must be an integer between 0 and 100 (issue #32 slice 2, decision 0025).

error.description: Optional reply line; omitted means the stage's default failure, and a present null is refused with 422 (decision 0044 §3). Omitted from answers when unset.

ChaosConfig.description: A null event clears that event's rule.

url.description: Must parse with an http:// or https:// scheme and a host to dial — refused at PUT otherwise (localhost:9000 is read as scheme localhost and is refused). Userinfo is sent as Basic authorization and stripped from every echo and log line

secret.description: An HTTP header value the delivery client accepts: at most 4096 octets, no control characters but tab, no leading or trailing space or tab; GET /api/v1/webhooks redacts it — PUT is the only writer

ca_pem.description: Optional PEM of an extra root CA to trust for this target, on top of the built-in root store
